critique_md:
The opening lands well. The tagline ("tiny in-memory LRU cache for TypeScript, zero deps, ~1KB gzipped") tells a first-time reader what they're looking at, who it's for, and where the tradeoffs sit — and the "When not to use this" section is the kind of honesty that earns trust. The Quickstart is also solid: a runnable basic block plus a realistic async-loader pattern, both copy-pasteable.

The single highest-impact gap is that there is no `Installation` section. A reader reaches the first code block before they know the package name to install. Add an `Installation` block immediately under the tagline with `npm i @acme/tiny-cache` (and the `pnpm` / `yarn` equivalents), plus the Node 18+ requirement that's currently buried under `Status`.

A secondary nit: the API surface is sketched (Features list, Options table) but the public methods — `get`, `set`, `has`, `delete`, `clear`, `keys`, plus the `onEvict` callback signature — are only visible through the example code. A short `API reference` section, or a link to generated docs, would unblock anyone past the Quickstart. There is also no `Contributing` guidance, so outside contributors have nowhere to start; even a one-line `CONTRIBUTING.md` link plus `pnpm test` in the README would help.
